_source: PRELIMINARY 2026-09-23. Prompts picked by Connor, adapted from Brian Parker's final Week 3 guide, '2026.09.27 Faith for Everyday Life Week 3.docx' (emailed 2026-09-22, 'final week 3 guide'), John 15:1-11. Rewritten as statement prompts, surface-level for a room of strangers: (1) from the guide's Background to the Text (vine imagery); (2) same section, reframed as a text question; (3) adapted from guide Q11 'What would you consider competing sources?', depersonalized to 'people'. QOTN not used as of 2026-09-23 (live AhaSlides) -- qotn field is a placeholder the renderer requires; ignore the -1-QOTN.png. #2 completed 2026-09-23 from John Slye's series email 'Sept. 13, 20, 27, Oct. 4' (2026-08-28), Week 3 big idea: 'The branch doesn't manufacture life. It stays connected to the source of life.' + guide Background ('the branch drew its sustenance and substance from the vine'). Oxford comma restored in #1 per Connor's wording. 2026-09-24: #3 rewritten by Connor verbatim ('Discuss common things that compete for your attention daily - How might what we focus on be shaping our identity and behavior?'); spaced hyphen set as em dash, 'How' lowercased after it. Echoes John's 9/27 outline line 'Show me what captures your attention every day, and I'll show you who you are becoming.'
questions: Share what you know about how vines, gardens, or pruning work.
Talk about why Jesus might have picked a vine to describe staying connected to him.
Discuss common things that compete for your attention daily — how might what we focus on be shaping our identity and behavior?
